task.description: WF-05 step 3, SECURITY-AUDITOR, dimension «security» of the part `docs`, audit AUD-002 (run AUD-002-20261122-01). SCOPE. Security of the documents of a PUBLIC repository (public on purpose since 2026-11-15, decisions/0111): docs/ (431 files), decisions/ (130), STATE.md, PLAN.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, tools/README.md, app/README.md, ideas/. Scope as the scout fixed it: secrets, identifiers, personal data and paths of a private computer in the 190 own files changed since AUD-001; nothing else of the Security row applies. Use scripts over the fixed copy (git grep) for key patterns (tokens, keys, passwords, connection strings, emails, phone numbers, IIN or similar personal numbers, user names, drive letters and home paths, internal hostnames, project and organisation identifiers) and then read every hit. Read docs/program/public-v1/PROGRESS.md line 17 (the Vercel organisation and project identifiers, marked there «not secret»): say whether the marking is right for each identifier. Check docs/owner-requests/, docs/business-plan/, docs/research/ and docs/archive/ for names of people, companies or numbers that should not be public. EXTRA CHECKS. (1) Q7: a secret value anywhere in git history of the changed documents is a Critical finding; give the file, the line and the commit, but never print the secret in the report (show the first 4 characters and the length) (2) the rule of the reference product: no name of the reference product may stand in any Sai file; report a hit as a finding without repeating the name in the report (3) the traces check (cd tools && npm run -s traces) is allowed and its result is evidence, but it is blind to Windows paths with backslashes (scout issue I4): search for them yourself NEEDS. The fixed copy <scratch>/aud002/tree (commit f72eaa7); read-only git (show, diff, log, grep, ls-tree against f72eaa7, e0a425b and the tags base/AUD-001-20261027-01 = b64562a and base/AUD-002-20261122-01); read-only gh; the scout's scope file for the passport of the part; the open defects in docs/issues/. NOT ALLOWED. On this PC: run npm run check, any npm script of tools/ or app/ that runs tests, node --test, the tools test scripts or the e2e tests; start Chrome; bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790; edit any project file other than your own report; commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. REPORT. Write your report to the file named in `output` (create the folder; JSON, 2-space indent, LF) as an object {audit:'AUD-002', part, dimension, role, subject:'f72eaa7', checked:[{check, how (the command or the files read), result}], not_checked:[{check, why}], findings:[...], summary}. A finding has the fields of WF-05 step 3: id (a short code like SEC-APP-01), check (what was checked; for requirements the requirement id and the criterion), severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low by WF-05 step 3), title, where (file and line), evidence (the command and its output, or a quote: a finding without evidence is not written), item (the bar item Q/R), recommendation (what exactly to fix and in which files). Severity by WF-05: Critical = a violation of a bar item that harms already now (a secret in files, invented events in Pixel Office, mixing of customer data, writing outside the own folder); High = a bar item not met or a criterion of a `done` requirement no longer met or a divergence from a recorded decision or a dependency with a known vulnerability; Medium = a document diverges from the files, a weak test, an outdated dependency without a known vulnerability; Low = names, dead code, formatting. Do not report a place that an open defect in docs/issues/ already covers: name the defect in `checked` instead. Do not pad: only real, evidenced findings; report what you could NOT check with the reason (this is not a finding and not a pass). In the `result` of your handoff write: verdict COMPLETED, the path of the report, the counts of findings by severity, the number of checks done and not done, and `issues` for anything ORCH or the owner must decide. The audit changes nothing in the project: your only files are the report and the result of your handoff. BE ECONOMICAL: the owner's usage limit is real. Prefer one script per group of checks, read files with targeted commands (grep, sed ranges, git show) instead of whole large files, keep narration short, and stop when the scope is covered. RULES OF THIS PC: FORBIDDEN here: npm run check, any npm script of tools/ or app/ that runs tests, node --test, the tools test scripts, the e2e tests, starting Chrome or any server on the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790 (a server started for a check binds port 0 and is stopped by its exact process id, AP-119); git commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset, tag; any edit of a project file other than the agent's own report. ALLOWED: reading the fixed copy of f72eaa7; read-only git and gh (gh run list, gh run view, gh run view --log, gh api GET); `cd tools && npm run -s traces` and `npm run -s handoffs-check`; the agent's own scripts and fresh clones only in its own folder under the scratchpad; Node 22 first on PATH (the Node 22 folder of this PC). WHAT REPLACES «COVERAGE-AUDITOR runs npm run check himself» (the dimension row of WF-05 is older than this PC rule): the agent READS the tests and the GitHub record of a run. The record of main is check run 44919421116 and app run 44919421105 (commit e0a425b, both success); the record of the head app/ is app run 45031353708 (app/ equal to f72eaa7); the work line has NO green record for tools/ (check runs 44875023688, 44875030768 and 45034277858 are red at handoffs-check, the fourth of six steps, so the steps test and e2e never ran for it). A tools file counts as covered by the record of main only when it is byte-equal between e0a425b and f72eaa7 (`git diff --name-status e0a425b f72eaa7 -- <file>` is empty, and the same for the test file and the helpers it imports); the diff is printed in the report. THIS RULE MAKES THESE FINDINGS «not checked: no record on GitHub for the work line» (never «met», never «not met»): (1) the result of any test that exercises a tools/ file that differs between main and the head (21 files of tools/, .github and .githooks, among them tools/src/node-floor.js, the REQ-110 guards, tools/src/team/cli.js, tools/src/web/main.js, tools/src/prepare.js, tools/src/handoffs/handoff.js, tools/src/picker/cli.js, tools/src/pixel-office/hook.sh, main.js, note.js, public/office-report.js, tools/test/e2e/run.js, tools/package.json); (2) every statement that the check of the work line passes; (3) tools/test/current-docs.test.js and the REQ-110 guards (no run has ever existed); (4) flakiness, duration, order dependence and any number that only a live run gives; (5) every criterion that needs a browser, a real Claude Code session (the owner's money, gate G2) or a reader and has no line in a record. A finding of severity Critical or High may rest only on something the agent read or ran itself (an allowed command, a file, a GitHub record line), never on a run it could not make. No report may print a secret (first 4 characters and the length only), a user name or a path of this PC (write paths relative to the project), or the name of the reference product. The report is the agent's own file; the project is only read. Your own folder for scripts and clones is <scratch>/aud002/<your-id> (the real path is in the message that launched you); the fixed copy of the project that is the SUBJECT of the audit is <scratch>/aud002/tree (a fresh clone at commit f72eaa7): read it, never edit it. Node 22 first on PATH (<node22>). Never write a path of this computer into your report or your handoff: write <scratch>, <node22> or <outside the project>. Never write the name of the reference product. One browser at a time on this PC and none is needed for your task unless the task says so.
